web_evidence.title: The Giver of Stars — official Penguin Books sample
web_evidence.note: The authorized 46-page sample sustains external third-person narration through the prologue and opening chapters, first focalizing Margery and then Alice; first-person forms occur only in speech or represented thought.

web_evidence.title: Extract: The Giver of Stars by Jojo Moyes
web_evidence.note: Publisher-hosted extract reproduces the prologue and Chapter 1 in sustained third-person narration, including external access to both Margery's and Alice's perceptions.

web_evidence.title: Jojo Moyes Writing Styles in The Giver of Stars
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly describes the novel as using third-person omniscient perspective across its dual-protagonist narrative.

person_note: The controlling narration is third person. The Goodreads material includes sustained passages that externally narrate Alice, Margery, Fred, and other characters while reporting their private perceptions; the many I, we, and you forms are overwhelmingly dialogue, aphorism, or quoted paratext rather than autonomous first- or second-person sections. Authorized Penguin prose independently confirms third-person narration in the prologue and opening chapters, and a whole-book point-of-view source explicitly describes a third-person omniscient dual-protagonist structure. No credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections was found; the only limitation is that the authorized web excerpts cover the opening rather than the entire novel.
